title: START - Stroke: Transition, Daily Life, Rehabilitation, and Participation - Perspectives of Stroke Survivors and Caregivers on Returning Home and Life at Home
summary:
Going home after a stroke can be difficult. Some people also find that they need more help with everyday life in the months or years that follow. We want to find out what makes it easier to return home and live there, where help is missing, and what supports people in making their own decisions and taking part in social life.
We will hold two guided group discussions by video in Germany and in Austria. People who have had a stroke, their family members, and people who support them in their work will share their experiences. Each discussion will last about 75 to 90 minutes, including breaks. Short questions, pictures, and enough time to respond will help people who find speaking or understanding difficult to take part. At the end, participants will say which improvements matter most to them. With everyone’s permission, we will record the sound. We will then write out the discussions and look for common themes and different experiences.
conditions: Long-term effects of stroke, including aphasia, and support needs during the transition from inpatient rehabilitation to home and while living at home in the longer term.

interventions.name: Prospective, multicentre, non-interventional qualitative study with two mixed focus groups, in Germany and in Austria. Approximately 12 to 16 adults will participate, with about 6 to 8 participants per group. The groups will include people living with the effects of stroke, including people with aph

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Lived experience of the effects of stroke, experience as a family member of a person living with the effects of stroke, or professional experience in providing care to people after stroke.
- Interest in taking part in a focus group.
- Sufficient German language skills to participate, with communication support as needed.
- Capacity to consent and written informed consent to participation, including audio recording.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent or lack of written consent to participation or audio recording.
Insufficient German language skills to participate despite the communication support offered.
An acute physical or mental health crisis that would make participation unduly burdensome despite breaks and support.
